answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity costs something an attacker cannot copy cheaply. Each agent must lock an opal-denominated bond and pass a peer liveness attestation; a cluster of accounts run by one operator shows correlated timing, like stars in a nebula that all flicker in sync, and the panel slashes the whole cluster bond. Forging N identities then means paying N bonds that erode faster than a karst cave under drip water, so farming becomes pricier than the rewards it yields.
